## Patient Information

### The aim of this leaflet is to give you information about corneal abrasion.

## **What is the cornea?**

### The cornea is the transparent dome shaped window of the eye. It is very sensitive, and has more nerve endings than anywhere else in the body.

## **What is a corneal abrasion?**

### A corneal abrasion is a scratch, which has damaged the surface of the cornea. This can be caused by any foreign object, which has come into contact with the corneal surface, for example:

###  grit

###  sand

###  paper

###  finger nail injury

## **What are the signs and symptoms?**

###  redness

###  pain

###  watering

###  inability to keep eyes open

###  feeling of something in the eye

## **What happens during the examination?**

### During an examination by an eye specialist with a high-powered microscope (slit lamp), eye drops will be put in to show the abrasion.

Page 2 of 2

## **What kind of treatment is given?**

### Antibiotic ointment is used for a prescribed time to the affected eye. We may ask you to make further visits to the clinic depending on the size of the abrasion.

## **How long will it take to heal?**

### Most abrasions are small and will heal very quickly within 24 – 48 hours. Oral analgesia (painkillers) such as paracetamol may be required for pain control, although this may not completely relieve the pain. Please remember if you suffer from:

###  increased redness

###  increased pain

###  vision gets worse

### contact your optometrist or if they are not available, your GP.

## **What happens when the abrasion has healed?**

### You may be asked to use a lubricating eye drop or ointment to help keep your corneal surface moist. Ointment is normally used at bedtime. This may have to be continued over a prolonged period of time to help prevent the condition recurring. This can happen if the corneal surface has failed to heal properly and your original symptoms may recur. Contact lens wearers will be asked to refrain from using these to the affected eye until discharged from the clinic.
